strand_a.summary: In recent years, the European Union (EU) has faced mounting challenges in promoting and safeguarding democracy in its neighbourhood, as autocratisation trends, entangled with intensifying geopolitical competition, have progressively reshaped the conditions under which EU democracy-support instruments operate. This article examines how the EU has responded to autocratisation in enlargement countries and states covered by the European Neighbourhood Policy (ENP), mapping the key actors involved and the instruments they deploy, including diplomatic engagement, political conditionality, sanctions, and support for civil society. dynamic_shocks.title: A conflict or blockade severs Europe's access to maritime trade routes
dynamic_shocks.plainly: Europe relies on maritime trade routes. Separate primary evidence shows that an armed-conflict escalation can change access quickly. Recent weak signals and historical material may strengthen the context, but neither can establish the shock on its own.
dynamic_shocks.second_order: Projects may keep their grants and institutions but still lose time, access or usable capacity while a replacement is found.
dynamic_shocks.why_easy_to_miss: The hypothesis appears when durable European capability evidence and a separately evidenced external pressure are read as one chain; low-weight current signals and history are then used only as context.
reasoning: Primary retained evidence shows European reliance on or expansion of maritime trade routes.
Separate primary retained evidence shows a live mechanism for an armed-conflict escalation.
Primary evidence contains 2 direct capability × pressure coupling record(s).
3 recent weak-signal item(s) point in the same direction; each is capped at 30% of a primary evidence item and none satisfies a primary threshold.
3 historical Strand-A item(s) provide structural context; they cannot serve as the current trigger.
The scenario becomes a shock only if the response is slower than the disruption.
conditions: Europe materially depends on maritime trade routes for current or planned work.
An armed-conflict escalation reaches the supplier, service, partner or rule that the European capability depends on.
Europe cannot substitute, reroute or absorb the change before projects begin losing usable capacity.
case_against: Recent media/weak-signal corroboration is intentionally down-weighted and cannot substitute for primary evidence.
The scenario still depends on the disruption arriving faster than Europe can respond.
prevention_actions: Plan alternative routes and inventories for chokepoint disruption.
Coordinate naval and commercial responses with partners.
Prepare alternative routes and suppliers before a conflict closes a corridor.
watch_for: A shipping route or supply corridor closes.
Insurers withdraw cover for a region.
dynamic_shocks.net_assessment: Well supported enough to watch closely, with contextual signals reinforcing rather than carrying the case.

page_guarantee.rule: New records update candidate reasoning; the shelf is re-decided each scan from recomputed maturity. No record takes a slot automatically.
page_guarantee.creative_reserve: Reserve = grounded runners-up + a creative reserve of relevant, uncontradicted hypotheses (distant, cross-domain, emerging, weak-signal or partially grounded), at least 18 and topped up toward 45, rotated across wow levels with weight on surprise. They mature into page competition when grounded.

high_order_inference.publication_policy: Stage 7 claim-native selection treats the reasoning layer as a future-hypothesis corpus. Candidate formation is broad; missing roles, thin evidence and unrun counter-evidence tests lower maturity rather than forbidding the hypothesis. Grounded candidates compete only within their wow 1-5 bucket. Each product reserves five public slots per wow level (25 maximum), displayed in repeated 5-4-3-2-1 order; surplus grounded findings remain reserve and weaker hypotheses remain developing.
high_order_inference.lifecycle_policy: Claim-native stock persists as page/reserve/developing tiers. Evidence is recomputed each scan; candidates can strengthen, weaken or move between tiers as new evidence arrives. Counter-evidence and falsifier results affect maturity and can kill a contradicted hypothesis, but an unrun challenge is not a ban on future-facing reasoning.
high_order_inference.candidate_search_policy: Missing-role and falsifier queries remain ordinary scanner discovery inputs and receive no admission waiver.
